utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1493, we stopped when we were discussing the referendum which you said necessarily took place following the failure of attempts to find a better solution. Do you remember the Izetbegovic/Gligorov plan? You mentioned that representatives of the republic, that is presidents of the republics, so all six republics had discussions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask that we focus on the questions for which I am a professional. I never was involved in politics, and I would ask that I not be asked political questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, if you can answer the questions, do, but we take note of what you say. Mr. Milosevic, there is little point in having a general political discussion with somebody who probably only has a general knowledge of it and no more. As we've said before, the important thing when cross-examining the witnesses is to concentrate on their evidence, the matters about which they can deal rather than general philosophical and political matters. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, the witness spoke about the referendum on the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and in his explanation, he said that efforts to find a political solution had failed, and now I'm asking him a question relative to what he himself said, why those efforts had failed. I asked him whether he remembers the Izetbegovic/Gligorov plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. And you've heard his answer. You've heard his answer. Yes. Let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the Cutilheiro plan, which, within the conference chaired by Peter Carrington, was adopted and signed by all three communities, Serbs, Croats and Muslims. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the plan very well, but I would like to say again that I wouldn't like to get involved in top-level politics because that was something that you were involved in. I was engaged in the profession about which I testified, and that is the area in which I should like to be questioned about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But since you mentioned the referendum and since you are a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, is there any dispute as to the fact that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, then and today, there are three constituent peoples living there, Serbs, Croats, and Muslims, and all three are recognised?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't need to spend a lot of time on this. This is a matter of general knowledge, not a particular matter for this witness, the fact that he mentioned the referendum is not a matter -- and at the moment I'm looking for the reference to it. Mr. Groome, can you help us? Where did he mention the referendum in his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you recall, I began to ask him about it and the Court advised me to not go into much detail because Court didn't find of it great assistance, so I don't think it was more than one question. I will work now and try to find the specific transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if we didn't find it of much assistance with the Prosecution, we're not going to find it necessarily a great deal of assistance as far as you're concerned, Mr. Milosevic. I do remember now. Yes. Ask the witness something he can give some evidence about, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Every citizen of Yugoslavia can testify about this, because we are talking about three constituent peoples, the Serbs, Croats, and Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're wasting time asking him general questions of this sort. You're taking your time up. It is, as you know, limited.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1493 explained, Mr. May, that this was, I don't know how to put it, a democratic act this referendum, so I'm asking him could a referendum held without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you insist on asking these questions which I have told you are irrelevant, then you're going to be stopped altogether in cross-examining. Now, it's a matter for you whether you're stopped or whether you go on. This witness's views about the referendum are of no assistance to the Trial Chamber. He gave a great deal of evidence. You should ask him about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I considered this to be a relevant question, that the referendum the witness mentioned was held without the participation of the Serbs, and you probably consider that is not relevant. So the Serbs are also not relevant in this whole matter except to be blamed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That will be a matter which we will have to determine in due course, but this witness can't give us any useful evidence about it. If it's a fact, it can be admitted and it will be something about which the Trial Chamber will have to consider, but arguing with the witness about it isn't going to help us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not arguing with the witness at all, but then let us move on with these questions that the witness testified about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr 1493, so you wish to limit yourself to military matters, so let me ask you then, since you described the group of volunteers from Serbia, the volunteers as some sort of special units, tell me, please, how did you describe the Mujahedin in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? What were they doing over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that in the first place, I did not describe the volunteers from the Republic of Serbia as volunteers, but I described them as special units, well trained, well prepared, and units that were under the command or, rather, under the control of the military leadership as is being proven now. As for this question of Mujahedins, I can guarantee in my area of responsibility there was not a single one operating or in existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know anything about, for instance, the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've given you my answer. In the area of my responsibility during the aggression on Bosnia and Herzegovina, not a single individual, not to mention a squad of them, was operating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but as a high-ranking officer of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I assume that you must have heard of the 7th Muslim Brigade. This is just one example.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim was not a brigade composed of Mujahedin. I will give you an answer, though you will probably be asking that question of someone from the area in which that brigade was. You are exaggerating when you say that there were I don't know how many thousand Mujahedin in Bosnia. I can tell you with full responsibility under oath that in that 7th Muslim Brigade, there were 250 to 300 men on the outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many passports of Bosnia and Herzegovina were issued to foreigners, to aliens?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would you deal with the matters which you know about, Witness B-1493. If you don't know, say so. There's no point, Mr. Milosevic, asking him something he may have he heard on the radio or something of that sort or read in the newspaper. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. It's a pointless exercise, although, no doubt, you want to do it because you want to repeat your case over and over again, but you're not to do it. You can ask the witness if he knows. Do you know about the issue of passports to foreigners, Witness B-1493?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do know that passports were issued, as I heard on television and over the radio, but I never saw anyone -- any single one being issued or by whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't even think that you participated in issuing passports, but I assume you must know about it as does everyone. In your statement, you say that the Serbs had taken control of Bijeljina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't take control of it. They occupied it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know what it looks like in translation, but that is one and the same thing. To occupy is a foreign word, and to take it, zauzeti, is a Serbo-Croatian word meaning the same thing. Tell me, please, do you know how many Serbs were living in Bijeljina before the beginning of the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the municipality of Bijeljina, according to the last census, had more than 50 per cent Serbs. So it was a municipality with a majority Serb population. But the town itself had a majority Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, how can it be that Serbs are taking Bijeljina and from whom are they taking Bijeljina from, a town in which they live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Bijeljina, as a town that was occupied by a special unit from the Republic of Serbia, was in the majority Muslim. The municipality of Bijeljina had a majority Serb population. Therefore, it wasn't the municipality that was occupied but exclusively the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that Serbs did not live in the town of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did. Certainly they did. They still do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course they do. Now, tell me, please, the commander of the Serb National Guard that was founded over there, this man Savic, Mauzer, is he from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mauzer is from the environs of Bijeljina. His unit was trained in the special training centre in Erdut, the Panthers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I held such a position as to be able to know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, do you know that this volunteer unit, the Serb Volunteer Guard of Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, had come there to assist upon the request of the local leadership and in an arrangement with Mauzer himself? Are you aware of that? A private arrangement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know at all that that unit had come at somebody's invitation. I know that that special unit came from the -- from another republic, another state, that it committed aggression. And in the initial stages, it was only this unit from the Republic of Serbia that participated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So there were no conflicts between the forces of the Green Berets and the Patriotic League which had blocked the town and the inhabitants of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there were no Green Berets in Bijeljina. Secondly, Bijeljina and the surroundings of Bijeljina, I explained that yesterday, I saw it, and I passed there, and I checked that area out. Bijeljina was blocked in a broad circle by units of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bijeljina was never blocked by JNA units, but JNA units were to be found everywhere as throughout Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I swear in this court that not a single road leading to Bijeljina was not accessible. Nothing could pass without being stopped and checked by members of the JNA and the Serbian guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards this volunteer unit, this happened later on, but are you familiar with the events in Bijeljina on the 31st of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to enter into the details regarding the incursion of the special unit from the Republic of Serbia, because this Court has already received an explanation about it and the number of dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards the number of dead, on the video film this somehow slipped in after the clips with the meeting between the general and Arkan. There were also a couple of bodies that slipped in. The first one that you saw is the woman whose name is Antonija, and she was a Serb woman who was killed in Bijeljina. And the other body is again a Serb. Let's not go into any further details because I've already tendered those photographs. Do you know those of your representatives of the Patriotic League of people and the Green Berets had killed in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the casualties in Bijeljina, we didn't count who was Serbs, who were Bosniaks, who were Croats. If we had counted the victims, I wasn't in Bijeljina when those victims fell, but I do know that one of the first victims was a Serb at the railway station when he didn't wish to -- he refused to stop when an Arkan man asked him to stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that Serbs killed Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. Arkan's men killed this Serb at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So the Serbs were killing Serbs in Bijeljina. Do you know how many were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was explained to you by the man who was in Arkan's unit and who was active in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did Mr. Gusalic, who testified here, do you know how the war in Bijeljina started when he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're not going to go through what some other witness said. It's not to the point. Now, you can ask this witness some questions which he can deal with, but it sounds to me as though it's all secondhand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who was in control of Bijeljina before the conflict, and do you know of the barricades in Bijeljina and the distribution of weapons to Muslims by Alija Suracevic, the president of the Bijeljina SDA from the mosque and the SDA headquarters in Njegosva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You don't know anything about that. And do you know of the existence of lists of Bijeljina Serbs for liquidation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you spoke of the plan and collecting data, in your statement you say that the order to collect data of this kind was also given to officer Ibrahim Hadzimustafic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement in connection with the collection of data regarding the plan, that you started your testimony, that with your colleague Ibrahim Hadzimustafic, an officer, also received the same assignment to collect data and prepare the plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we didn't collect any data. We were working on it. The name you mentioned was my drawer. He was a draughtsman in my team. He was a draughtsman. That was his position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's an officer, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A reserve officer. A lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim like you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could that be evidence that nothing was done on a discriminatory basis in that regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the plan I mentioned, I was replaced, dismissed from my duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you perhaps replaced because did you not intervene with that joint detachment of yours according to those people who caused the fires or whatever or were you replaced for the reasons you gave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably wasn't replaced for the reasons you gave me Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. because after me not a single officer --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Out of an abundance of caution, could I ask the Chamber to inquire from the witness whether the fact that his colleague's name said publicly whether that's going to compromise the protections that the Court has given him. I don't the answer to that, but it seems that it might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, are you asking for it to be redacted rather than go through --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Rather than go through this. Yes, we'll redact that. Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As you say on page 3, paragraph 1 of your statement, that non-Serb officers were replaced and sent to occupy less important positions, do you happen to know how many non-Serb officers there were in your own corps, not to mention the name of the corps or anything else to avoid having you identified. But how many non-Serb officers were there in your own corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my corps, let me say there were quite a lot of non-Serb officers, but most of them occupied less important positions. And that's what I said yesterday. So none of the commanders, the chiefs of staff or assistance or battalion commanders, brigade commanders from 1991 were non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not true, but answer me this, please: How many Serbs were there in the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time that you joined up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my own -- in the unit I commanded, there were about 4.8 per cent of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 4.8 per cent, is that what you said? On page 2, paragraph 4, you say that after the withdrawal of the JNA from Croatia and Slovenia, the JNA units deployed mostly in areas where the Serb population was dominant. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Serbs hostile towards the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They accepted the JNA. They were friendly disposed towards them while it was the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You personally, as an officer of the JNA, did you feel more secure, safer where there was no -- there were no hostilities expressed towards the JNA, no hostile sentiments towards it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the JNA you say. Well, as I say, while it was the JNA, a popular people's army, we all felt proud of being part of the JNA. After 1990, the officers who were non-Serbs did not feel comfortable in that same army. We were humiliated. We were dismissed from our jobs. You took away our five-pointed star insignias, replaced them with Serb flags and so on. Our conversations were listened in to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't in charge of the JNA, so I didn't take the insignias away. The fact that you changed them is your affair. But tell me this: Did you know of the phenomenon based on a political directive which came from the very peaks of the Democratic Action Party, from Alija Izetbegovic himself, that Muslim recruits were leaving the JNA or should leave the JNA and should not respond to the call-up for mobilisation and to go and join up into the units of the JNA? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never a member of the SDA party myself, but I do know that a member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, in fact, by virtue of his office forbid or brought in a directive by which the Territorial Defence units could not be deployed in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, and that the recruits should not respond to the mobilisation call-up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah, that they should not respond. Were are you talking about the Serbisation of the JNA if the Serbs responded to the call-up for the mobilisation whereas in Bosnia-Herzegovina the Muslims and Croats, following a political directive, failed to respond to the call-up for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina and its recruits did not wish to take part in the aggression either against Slovenia or against Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I like to hear that they were aggressions. Now, tell me this: From what I can see in your statement on page 3, paragraph 9, you refer to the Serb Crisis Staff and say that you heard of it for the first time in March 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the reasons for which the Serb Crisis Staff was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Crisis Staffs were set up on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and before that in Croatia quite a long time before. The SAO Posavina. So these Serb territories. That's where they were. And they were formed on a purely ethnic basis and level, including all the Serbian insignias, the Serbian flag was flown from municipality buildings and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In the alleged arming of the Bosnian Serbs by the JNA, did the Muslims take part in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably found one paragraph where I state that somewhere towards the end of -- let me just remember this correctly. That a large column turned up which was brought in by Hadziefendic, Hasim from Belgrade, that they -- he spent the night in my place in the barracks and then took the column after to Banja Luka to resupply the rocket brigade, to resupply it with rockets. And let me just finish what I was saying. That gentleman is married to a woman from Loznica. He remained in the army of Yugoslavia. He was promoted during the aggression between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the rank of general and performed a high function in the General Staff of the army of Yugoslavia and he lives in Belgrade today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So effected the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, did he? All right. Fine. Now, tell me this: During the time you spent working in the JNA, your service in the JNA and the period you're testifying about, was the JNA the sole legitimate armed formation, and I would like to emphasise the word legal, lawful.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army was the sole legal armed force on the territory of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me whether the legal and legitimate operation of repositioning its officers from one place to another, including the Territorial Defence, which was within its composition, was that all right too? And we cleared that up yesterday. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it legal to transfer certain units from one place to the other of that sole legal armed force on the territory of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was legal. But it was not legal to transfer and pull out the Yugoslav People's Army from the area of Slovenia, from the whole of the territory of Slovenia. That isn't legal. Neither was it legal to hand over the Varazdin Corps which was the best-armed corps without a single bullet having been fired. It was not legal to hand over the Rijeka Corps without a single bullet being fired either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me about the Varazdin Corps? They?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know who they did surrender to; to the members of the Croatian guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many blockades were set up, blockades of the barracks and attacks on the barracks of the JNA throughout Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about that, but the Varazdin Corps was very strong and was able to resist all those blockades had there been the interest of doing so. It could have solved that problem had it really been interested in doing so. And that's why you brought that corps commander to trial in Belgrade and he was found guilty and sentenced to I don't know how many years in prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. I asked you whether the JNA had attacked Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Croatia or was it that the Croatian paramilitaries attacked the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA attacked Croatia. The first beginnings of the aggression in Croatia were precisely what I said in my statement yesterday. From Mirkovci, Jankovci and the infiltration of Seselj's White Eagles, introducing general chaos in Croatian towns. Then the JNA would turn up and little by little occupy it. That's how it all began and that's what happened in Vukovar too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But don't the facts tell us otherwise, Mr. 1493 or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information or data tells us how it was in Bosnia-Herzegovina, With Bijeljina, with Zvornik, with Brcko the same thing happened. You know what happened in Brcko, the slaughter that took place there. Not the JNA, but you first infiltrated the paramilitary formations or special purpose units, the specials. And they had lists and were ordered to arrest all professors, doctors, well to do and respected people, to loot them too, and then the JNA took control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1493, I'm not asking you that. This isn't the right place for political propaganda about an alleged aggression, the alleged aggression of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's one of the crucial issues isn't it, Mr. Milosevic that you've been raising as to how this matter started. So the witness is entitled to give evidence about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May, fine. So witnesses do have the right to make political speeches, do they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The evidence about the start of the aggression, Mr. Milosevic. That's extremely relevant, I should have thought. You've certainly raised it. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, tell me this: Can paramilitary units be those who are within the composition and under the command of the JNA? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA was established according to its formation and structure, and anything that did not belong to that formation and establishment was paramilitary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If there is a volunteer unit under the command of the JNA, for example, by law and according to the law on defence of Yugoslavia, it too belongs to the defence forces of Yugoslavia, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the strategy of armed struggle which was in force at the time, it did not provide for any paramilitary volunteer units of any kind. But the defence of Yugoslavia was in the hands and based on the use and deployment of the Yugoslav People's Army, the Territorial Defence, and the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine, Mr. 1493, but you know full well that the law also provides for the fact that everybody who defends Yugoslavia by -- through arms and its territorial integrity is to be part and parcel of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is an individual who is conjoined with a formation of the JNA or Territorial Defence. He cannot under any conditions be outside those formations. Anything outside those formations is considered to be unlawful and not legal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me this: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina whose member you were, was it legal or illegal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina of which I was a member was the sole legal armed force on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me this: The army of Republika Srpska, was it legal or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of the Republika Srpska was an illegal formation on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was only the Muslims who had the right to bear arms in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a civil war; is that right? As far as the Serbs, they did not enjoy that same right, and I assume the HVO was an illegal formation, too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have told you that the unit under my command, that I had a brigade unit commander who was a Serb. I had [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] May that be struck from the record, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How come that conflict, the conflict that took place at different times, different periods between the Serb forces, Muslim forces and Croatian forces and so on and so forth, how come you consider only the Muslim forces to be legal forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was not an army of the -- was not a Muslim army. The Bosnia-Herzegovina army was made up of all three ethnic groups living on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and all three ethnic groups fought within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the territorial integrity of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know facts and figures about how many Muslims there were in the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many thousands, I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only those who had to protect their families had joined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those who had to be recruited for their families' sakes, did they sign up to be directors, leaders, functionaries, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I precisely quoted the example of the man who held a high rank, a general in the Yugoslav army. He brought in the rockets and missiles, and I believe that he stayed on in the army not because he liked to stay on but in order to protect and safeguard his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you drew that kind of observation and logic for the thousands of Muslims what made up the army of Republika Srpska, and that logic does not hold true for that handful of Serbs who were in the Bosnia-Herzegovina army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's me repeat. The handful -- there was not a handful of Serbs in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I can tell you the numbers, quote the figures if need be in the unit under my command, for example. So it was not just a handful of men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said 4.8 per cent. That was the figure you quoted, and that -- such a small number comes under the statistical error type of figure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figure is 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but that negligible figure is considered a statistical error. Now, as you say that the JNA occupied towns and villages, how can it occupy places where it had been present for the past 50 years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the Yugoslav People's Army no longer was because a people's army. It had lost all the attributes of a popular army when it withdrew from Slovenia. Once it had withdrawn from Slovenia, it was no longer of the Yugoslav People's Army, no longer a popular national army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say that the non-Serb population had to be left without their leading figures, without their leaders; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every plan had lists of persons who in the first stages, in the initial phase should have been arrested and killed by the specials. And Brcko is a fine example of this where about 3.000 intellectuals were killed in the space of just several days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, come on. That kind of information nobody has ever heard of. Nobody has heard of facts and figures like that. But tell me this: As you say that there were plans to behead and leave it without its leaders tell me where you got that information from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information comes from the political leaders, from the political peaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean from your political peaks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That those lists exist can be seen from the fact that it wasn't Ilija or Hasan who should be killed seeing to their land, but it was professors, doctors, and engineers which were to have been liquidated, and Brcko, Prijedor, are good examples.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, which Yugoslav officer anywhere issued orders to that effect, orders of that kind which implied the liquidation of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. intellectuals and respected citizens, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those lists were compiled by members of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But how do you know or how can you claim -- how do you dare say -- where do you get the audacity to state that the plans were planned in the 2nd military district and there was a secret agreement between the JNA and the local SDS? And you state that on page 4 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a list of highly respected individuals, the inhabitants of a town, and that list was compiled by the SDS, and it contained the names of individuals to be liquidated in the first stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they liquidated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't, because the town wasn't occupied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw a list of persons up for liquidation but they weren't liquidated. Fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the town was not occupied in the final instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me who took part in these agreements on the part of the SDS? Who represented the SDS? Who represented the JNA? If you know anything about those agreements at all, then you must have some knowledge about who, on behalf of the SDS, did this and who, on behalf of the JNA, did this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of 1992 into the command in which I myself went, that is to say from February up until April when the events in Bijeljina were unleashed, there were daily visits by the most highly responsible persons in the SDS came to visit the command headquarters. I myself did not have access nor did any lower-ranking officers have access to the command but people had daily meetings about what was going to be done and the events that were to come to pass. And I state in my statement -- I quote some of the names there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give me some names now? Could you name some names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could, but may we go into private session for that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please on page 4, paragraph 8, you say -- I won't mention the name of the corps but the appropriate command of the JNA of that corps did not have any command over Arkan's unit during the conflict in Bijeljina. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I said, because if he had had command over it, then he wouldn't have allowed that unit to do what it did. So when that unit arrived from Serbia, it did not resubordinate itself to the corps, but it carried out orders that it received from someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned Biljana Plavsic in Bijeljina and you showed her on this tape. Was she an official of Serbia or Bosnia-Herzegovina? Was she a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you listen to my statement, that is what I said, that Biljana Plavsic, as a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with the authority to authorise force, instead of giving orders at least to the police if to no one else, which was very powerful in Bijeljina, to arrest those Arkan's men, she embraces him and congratulates him on the misdeeds he had committed. That is what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But tell me, didn't a Serbian member of the Presidency and a Muslim member of the Presidency come together, that is, Biljana Plavsic and Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I said yesterday. On the right there was Fikret Abdic, Lieutenant Colonel Prasovic, and on the left, Biljana Plavsic. You can see them walking together. Let me add, Fikret Abdic, when he came to Bijeljina his car was stopped. He and his two escorts were forced to lie down. They were thoroughly searched and only then was he allowed to join in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you think that Biljana Plavsic could have issued orders as a member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina to any police or military unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police was under the authority of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The police was within the competence of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Surely you know that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. So that Biljana Plavsic could have called up the prime minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina and given him that order. She had the authority to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me, are you really claiming that this general who was in fact Chief of Staff as far as I know, of the 2nd Military District, reported to Arkan in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please find somewhere this? He went towards Arkan. He stopped. He saluted him, and then he congratulated him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a moment, please. Why are you talking about reporting? How can someone who is coming -- arriving be reporting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has explained what he meant, and there didn't seem to be any point going on. We've seen the video. We don't need to go on about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, that is what I'm saying. Why is he calling it reporting? How could it be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have seen the video. We have heard his evidence. There is no need to take any further time or waste time on it. Let's move on. Don't bother to answer any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What is the general manner of greeting somebody when one is wearing a uniform and has a cap on his head? Doesn't an officer greet everyone in that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. The difference between reporting and a greeting is a drastic one. Take the tape and review it. When you're reporting to someone, somebody reporting to somebody else who is coming, he has to stop at a distance of three or five steps. He has to stand at attention and salute. Then this other one approaches and greets him. And you will be able to see that on that tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't explained that, but apparently Mr. May insists that you have explained it and we will have occasion to hear other witnesses who know more about it. Very well. Just give me a yes or no answer to save time. Did JNA members take part in the fighting in Bijeljina in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time that Arkan arrived, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The whole war in Bijeljina lasted four days. There was no fighting after that. Therefore, did members of the JNA take part in any kind of fighting at any time in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the expulsion of the population from Bijeljina, members of the JNA participated in searching of houses, expulsions, lootings, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that members of the JNA searched houses and looted them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police went there, individuals, groups. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1493, there are so many witnesses from Bijeljina. How can you claim such a thing? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that, but I can claim that with certainty on the basis of what the people said who were exchanged from the Batkovic camp and who came to our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll hear those men. It is quite contrary to the information that I have here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the process only in Bijeljina. In Prijedor and Banja Luka as well. The JNA occupied Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Regarding the reporting that you refer to, isn't it logical that he could have only reported to the general and not the other way round?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're stopping wasting time like this. Now, you've got about 20 minutes left. I suggest if you have any more important questions you go on to them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. I really do have quite a number of questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a senior officer of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and later in view of the positions you held, were you aware that in Sarajevo at the end of June 1991 a rally was held at which only Muslims were present, members of various parties of Islamic orientation? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know anything in connection with the establishment of the so-called Council for National Defence which later became the political wing of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take part in that, nor am I aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time he was already a former JNA officer and later commander of the Main Staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sefer Halilovic was never the commander of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, not commander, Chief of Staff. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what we're talking about, Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he entrusted with the ideological shaping of the army, the defence plan of Sarajevo and the Sarajevo region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sefer Halilovic can never be entrusted as an individual with such a task. A whole team of people has to do such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But we have his statement too. Then it is easy to establish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did head the team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As this was happening in June 1991, tell me, who attacked Sarajevo in June 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sarajevo was not attacked in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well then what kind of a military organisation of the so-called defence of Sarajevo was being worked on in Sarajevo in June at this gathering of exclusively Islamic organisations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And don't you think then that on the pretext of the defence of Sarajevo an aggressive fundamentalist organisation was being formed which later called itself the Patriotic League of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that because I did not participate in it at the time. I was never a member of the Patriotic League or the Green Berets. Let me tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that before Sefer Halilovic the drafting of the plan on the so-called defence of Sarajevo was rejected by also former senior officials in the JNA who were Muslims, General Sarac, Safet Hadzic, Azim Hodzic, who were offered also this task of organising this, and they refused?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: See if the witness knows anything about what you're asking. Do you know anything about this allegation? It's a suggestion which the accused is making. Do you know anything about it? Other than what you might have read in the papers or seen on the television.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know anything about that. I only know as much as the other citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina or citizens of Yugoslavia know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, move on to something that he can deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all about a meeting many months before any conflict broke out attended by Izetbegovic, Halilovic, Munir Jakic, Resad Bekic, Safet Hadzic, as president of the Crisis Staff of Sarajevo, Mirsad Kemo, Zeljko Pudza, and when the Main Staff of the Patriotic League was named? Do you know anything about those events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about it, nor have I heard of such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me now, please, as this plan is something I'm not aware of, what is the plan called RAM, R-A-M?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my statement that I never saw it. I heard of it but I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you heard about that RAM plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it exists. All I can explain now to you is that the RAM plan, and I repeat that I never saw it nor was directly involved in it. But I had worked on war planning ever since 1988, at a very high level and it now prompts me to recall a plan that was not called RAM but had roughly the same borders and the same roles. Namely, in 1988, the political and military leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia decided to disband the 9th army in Slovenia and disband the 7th army in Bosnia-Herzegovina and to form the 5th Military District based in Zagreb and the 1st Military District based in Belgrade. The 1st military district has borders exactly along the line that the Greater Serbia was interested in. Those were the borders of the 1st Military District, that is, along the lines Virovitica-Karlobag. And the deployment of those unit were such -- so I hadn't seen this plan RAM but plan S2 is a plan I worked on for nights and months. The distribution of cause was such that the Novi Sad Corps was between the rivers of the Drava and the Sava right up to Virovitica. You asked me. Allow me to answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was is not my question. We will just be spending time. Your corps covered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness finish. Just explain if you would so the Court -- so the Court can understand. What is the connection of what you're saying with the RAM plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't believe you will be able to hear this from other witnesses because this is something I worked on, on this plan. According to this plan S2, the Novi Sad Corps would be between the Drava and Sava rivers. I don't have a map here, so just south of Virovitica up to the Sava River. Then below it comes -- below that corps was the Tuzla 17th Corps reaching the line roughly Slunj, Glina. Then below it would come the 5th Banja Luka Corps north of Prijedor in Croatia, and then further down there's the Knin Corps, which was not part of the 5th Military District but remained in the military naval district but was on the border along this line of interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What -- so we can follow, what is the point that you're making of the similarity between -- of the S2 plan with the RAM plan? What did you understand the purpose to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there are two similarities or, rather, identical features. The first, the area of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. responsibility of the 1st Military District, the Belgrade district, coincides fully with the plan RAM, the north-western border of plan RAM. Secondly, the deployment of units of the 1st Military District according to the S2 plan fully coincides with the plan RAM and the interests --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1493, let me cut short your pains. This plan RAM does not exist. It's a code for switching over to a coded conversation. And what you're talking about, three military districts and how they covered the whole of Yugoslavia, this is common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will this be redacted, please? I want this redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But didn't you say that this reorganisation of the military districts was carried out in 1988?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what organisation are you talking about as a function of any type of Greater Serbia? You're talking about 1988 and the reorganisation of the Yugoslav People's Army into the three areas and the distribution of the whole territory that way, the internal organisation of the Military-Naval Sector and the RVPVO. That was the JNA. So what Greater Serbia are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I am saying is that with the disbanding of the 7th Army District and it being joined up to the 1st Army district, that the north-westerly boundaries of the 1st Military District coincide with the boundaries of the Greater Serbia which was where the interests lay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you hear anything about a Greater Serbia from? Did you ever hear from any officials of Serbia or Yugoslavia of a plan for a Greater Serbia? Did you ever hear anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just heard about it quite a bit in the political speeches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any functionary in power in Serbia and Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who then? Give me a name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seselj many times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Seselj was in the opposition until 1997. I'm asking you about officials in power.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall his speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on not to waste time. You say you know nothing about all this. In the summary on page 2, point 8 of your statement, you refer to the Patriotic League of peoples as a group set up by non-Serb civilian authorities and the local population; isn't that right? Take a look at the summary, point 8 of your summary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Patriotic League? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You say a group set up by non-Serb civil authorities and the local civilian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was never a member, nor did I take part in the creation of the Patriotic League nor was a member of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how then is this mentioned in your summary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know anything about the Patriotic League as being formed as a paramilitary formation of the SDA in the spring of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I did not take part in the establishment of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you took part in its formation. I'm asking whether you know about it, know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't. Right. Now, later on, do you know anything about the fact that it had nine military districts, subregional headquarters and staff at lower levels, municipal levels, headquarters after those lower-down levels? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the start of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Bosnia-Herzegovina we had the Ministry of Defence which stayed intact as it did before the aggression. And there were Territorial Defence Staffs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the beginning of the aggression which was -- which took over the role and continued working as it had done before the aggression. So that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as far as the Territorial Defence is concerned and the Ministry of Defence or ministries of defence, prior to the aggression and after the aggression no changes -- there were no changes at all. The Defence Minister stayed the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know that what you say, that it was formed by the local inhabitants, that this 10th subregional headquarters was in Serbia -- Serbia in Novi Pazar, covering Novi Pazar, Tutin, Sjenica, Prijepolje, Varos, and Priboj on the territory of Serbia as well as Klevja [phoen], Bijelo Polje on the territory of Montenegro? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know that this was formed in the spring of 1991, as early on as that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there were manoeuvre units and special platoons for terrorist activities and sabotage, that they were formed? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the frameworks of the Patriotic League of people's or nations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in the area, and there was no such unit there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you occupied positions that you did, that you say you did, do you know that all these regional and subregional staffs and headquarters were formed precisely by Sefer Halilovic using forged ID cards, for example, Mirsad Tucin [phoen], a Muslim, and a Croat, and a Serb ID card, that in his travels he resorted to forged ID cards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Territorial Defence where I was, I was not appointed by Sefer Halilovic but by the Defence Minister Doko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this now, please: Do you know who was responsible for planting an explosive device at the mosque in Novi Sarajevo, in Novi Sarajevo, or, rather, do you know -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The witness given evidence about this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he mentioned the Patriotic League of Nations, and they were precisely responsible for doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is a waste of time. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that the sabotage terrorist units of the Patriotic League of Peoples --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us establish --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Forcibly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- There was such a unit or the witness knows anything about it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. I'm going to deal with this. It's alleged that the Patriotic League had a sabotage terrorist unit. That's the allegation which is made by this accused. Do you know anything about any such unit or whether there's any truth there that sort of allegation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honours, I say with full responsibility that in the area of responsibility which was under my command, and that was the largest area in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was not a unit of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your area of responsibility, the road Visegrad-Uzice to Dobrun, did that come under your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then I won't asking you anything about that. Do you know how these formations were armed, the units set up in the spring of 1991 on the Muslim side? Do you know how they were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to speak about a Muslim side or a Serb side or a Croatian side. If you want to talk about these matters then we can speak about it as being the Territorial Defence at the beginning and later on the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And what I can tell you is this: After I left the JNA and joined the Territorial Defence, that in that area you would not be able to rally a company with any arms, even hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we've heard that story, but I don't know who killed all the Serbs in Bijeljina with those hunting rifles that you mention. But do you know that all the business of arming the Patriotic League and the paramilitary formations in general was done by -- Alija Izetbegovic gave this job to Hasim Cengic who was a member of the political leadership of the PNL, and he was later the Defence Minister too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you know anything about what the accused is talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything. All I can say is that Hasan Cengic was never the Defence Minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're wasting your time asking questions about which the witness knows absolutely nothing. You're wasting the time of the Court and taking up the time of your cross-examination. You have five minutes left. So if you've got any important questions, you should ask them instead of these political ones.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have quite a number of questions left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know that Sefer Halilovic himself, in statement he made to the investigators of that other side over there, as far back as 1996, said that the Patriotic League, later the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, obtained its weapons in such a way as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How can he know about what somebody said to the investigators, apart from what he said himself? I'm going to consult as to whether we shouldn't bring all this to a conclusion. You're using the occasion to make political points, and it seems to be a complete waste of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. This is not a political --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. You've got five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I was asking you was this: Did you know about the theft and looting of weapons from the JNA warehouses that were carried out, as Mr. May interrupted me a moment ago, which were carried out on the basis of what Sefer Halilovic himself said? Do you know about this taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that after the events in Bijeljina, you joined the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you joined up on the 10th of April; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you say in your statement. After the Serbs took control of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, then. Is this what is true, that on that day, on the 10th of April, 1992, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established and that that was the sole reason that you left the JNA on that particular date and not the fact that Bijeljina had been taken control of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true that the BH army was formed on the 10th of April, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want to tell me -- if you want me to tell you when it was formed, I'll have to hurry up and go back home because it celebrates its anniversary. It was formed on the 15th of April, 1992, in fact. So that you should know that fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you joined the BH army five days before it was actually established. Right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like this to be redacted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What has that got to do with it? I'm not asking you about your own name. I'm asking you about something else and someone else. Mr. 1493, is it true that already in the month of June 1992. BH army within its composition had 230.000 soldiers of which the 2nd Corps, for example, numbered 70.000 men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this in private session? Could this be stricken from the record?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain to us why it should be in private session. It doesn't identify you in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... And then see what the difficulty is, but we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this: Is it true, in view of the fact that from the -- you were in the army from its very inception, the so-called army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that already in June 1992 it numbered 230.000 men bearing arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how many men did it have? Could you be so kind as to tell us? And this is something that we can check easily. We can check out what you're saying and what actually happened according to the facts and figures.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak about the unit I was in, the unit that I was head of at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how can you then say that it is not correct if you don't know? You can say you don't know, not that it's not correct. Because now you say that you can only vouch for your own unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about my own unit which was best armed. All the other units had less weapons than my own unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me how many men your unit had then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. Because.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Mr. May, the witness is duty-bound to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer it in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you weren't listening. The witness has just explained that the number I mentioned for the Bosnia-Herzegovina army was not correct, and then he said he could only vouch and tell us for his own unit. Then I asked him whether he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will go into private session and then we're going to bring this cross-examination to an end. Yes, let's go into private session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is the submission of the amici that this last document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Regarding all the matters I asked in private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Give it the next C number. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is also our submission in view of the significance of this document, in our judgement, without mentioning the names, I think that this should be heard in open session too without mentioning names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think we need go over it again. The matter's been dealt with. It's on the record and we've heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any event, if you accept the document, it should be known what the documents are about, because these are court documents, official documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There is no need to go over it again. The matter has been put before the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, during the examination-in-chief yesterday, you said that the war in Croatia started in the night between the 7th and 8th of May, 1991. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never mentioned the 7th and 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What is the date then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk about the beginning of the war in Croatia at all. I just spoke about the situation that I was in in the period from the 2nd of May until the 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that serious armed conflicts started after the proclamation of independence by Slovenia and Croatia at the end of June? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mention that in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you. Do you know that in view of the job you performed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know what happened in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened after that regarding the blockade of barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All over Croatia. You were then active, up until April 1992. Did you know what the army experienced during the period of that year while you were still a member of the army. Do you know that at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that all the barracks were under blockade? You mentioned the Varazdin barracks a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blocked by unarmed people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no fire opened on barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Varazdin Corps did not respond to that fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Varazdin Corps had a Armoured Brigade with 96 tanks, and they did not react. Not a single tank fired a single shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is why that general was held responsible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you now something in connection with the document we were dealing with yesterday and which you read out upon the request of the Prosecutor. That is tab 2 of Exhibit 425. If you remember, you read out yesterday a part of it, the last sentence, and you said when the Prosecutor asked you in connection with the last sentence that the reference, in fact, was to the fact that the commander cadres, the military leaders, had to concern themselves with the protection of the lives of soldiers. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I think it says to be able to protect manpower. It meant its own personnel and not the people in its area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. To protect the soldiers themselves. That was my understanding too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the previous sentence of that same document which is dated the 4th of April, 1992, you were still in the army, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read it out to you, what it says here so as to spare you the trouble. It is the paragraph on forecasts, and it says: "In the days to come, a further deterioration is expected over the overall security and political situation. Inter-ethnic conflicts in Posavina and Semberija threaten to escalate and spread to other parts of the zone of responsibility with the possibility of very tragic consequences, human casualties, and material damage. Armed provocations are possible of commands and units as well as attacks on military warehouses and isolated facilities by paramilitary formations." Under those circumstances, as well as in the other situations when barracks were surrounded during the time you were still in the Yugoslav People's Army, did the army invest maximum efforts to avoid unnecessary casualties and damage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not a single barracks was surrounded because everything was moved out from places where the majority were Muslims or Croats in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to ask you about. Was there attack on the army when it was pulling out in Sarajevo, and in other places too? Were the soldiers endangered and attacked though they weren't attacking anyone when they were pulling out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're claiming that in Bosnia, barracks were not blocked. For instance, in Sarajevo itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, there was no blockade of barracks but of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
