utterances.text: Were there any casualties among soldiers who were jeopardised outside the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will see from the tape provided by the commander of the 2nd Military District, it is not at all correct what is being claimed. Six people were killed in that column. You will be able to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But let's go back to the document I'm holding in my hand. In point 2, you read it up to the middle, and I would like to read the rest of it for you. "The influence can be felt of SDS and Arkan's propaganda which leads to the departure of soldiers from the unit with weapons." Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Virtually from the events in Slovenia and then in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was large-scale desertion. Even parents went to fetch their sons, their recruits from the army. And this went on literally until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, since you were an officer, that from the moment the problems arose in the area of Yugoslavia in those days, that the main problem was related to the military and state leadership as to how to make an appropriate decision to deprive paramilitary units of weapons? Is that so or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not. I see. Let me now ask you a few more questions in connection with your evidence. You said that on the 10th of April, you left the JNA because it was no longer a people's army. So it was on the 10th of April, 1992, after the Serbs had captured Bijeljina that you left JNA, because as you say, it was no longer a people's army. In other words, it means that you thought it was a people's army up until that moment. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We officers, particularly Bosniak officers, considered the Yugoslav army to provide security for us, and we wanted to live in that common state. But however, the sequence of events from Slovenia onwards gradually deprived the Yugoslav People's Army of those characteristics. So it no longer existed until when it withdrew from Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were a member until 1992 and only then you realised it was no longer people's army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I realised that long ago because I didn't perform any serious duties by then. And there were other reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I wanted to ask you, when you left the Yugoslav People's Army, did you believe that you had the good luck that in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the beginning of war there were plenty of both active and reserve officers who stood up in defence of defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina so that the [redacted] region and all other regions, not only that of [redacted]--

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this being redacted, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes. There's that one word, yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Groome, there is a great deal of confusion at the moment in this evidence. The witness seems to have the idea that he can ask for whatever hearing he wants. Now, I don't know how he got that notion. No doubt it's the fault of the Court for allowing it to happen. But future witnesses must be disabused in this. Now, I cannot see -- we'll go into private session. We'll go into private session, and we'll deal with the matter. But it's -- it is very unsatisfactory to have a hearing in which this kind of process is taking place all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here is what you said in your statement to the investigators on the 20th of April, 2002. "In May 1992, JNA units who remained in Bosnia-Herzegovina were just renamed into units of the army of Republika Srpska. Those were the only changes that took place." Is that precisely what we were just saying, that the Serbs from Bosnia and Herzegovina who were living there now were simply renamed into soldiers and officers of the army of Republika Srpska? Did the same apply to your own units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. JNA units who found themselves in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina were renamed the army of Republika Srpska. All the commanders and all units, 80 per cent of the manpower remained in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Only a part of the anti-air defence units, whereas all the other units remained in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and all officers were receiving their salaries from the budget of Yugoslavia until perhaps a year ago. And the present Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska is a retired general of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago, you said that you heard for the first time in March 1992 of Serbian Crisis Staffs. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But here in your statement, you said earlier on, "I have no information about the participation of the SDS and the Serbian MUP in the formation and organisation of these Crisis Staffs. I also have no information of the involvement of officers of the 17th Corps or other officers of the JNA." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also right that you have no information of officers of the state security in the JNA? That's what you said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I have no information about the participation of the Serbian MUP? I didn't get your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is contained in your statement. Do you remember saying that? And you also said: "As for the role of the MUP, I can say that most Serbian members of the MUP of BH left a certain place after the events in Bijeljina in April 1991 and went to territory under the control of Bosnian Serbs where they formed the Serbian MUP within the framework of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct, that you have no information regarding the involvement of the army of Yugoslavia when Srebrenica fell in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That also is correct, because I wasn't in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two objections that I would like to be recorded while the witness is here present. The first objection relates to you. Namely, you refused any word to be uttered in open session in connection with a court document referring to war crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's absolutely right. It's on the court record. What's your second objection?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to say that this witness, in his public evidence, spoke about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We're not here to listen to speeches from you. You've had a very long cross-examination. We have ruled on the matter you've raised. Now, if you've got a second objection, make it, or we're moving on to re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My second objection, which I also wish to be entered in the record, has to do with the fact that this is now, according to my records, the 38th or 39th witness already, and I'm sure there will be more, who is denying what is stated in his statement. And he gave the statement on the 20th of April, 2002, and he denied that he ever said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We hear what you say. It is not a matter for -- to interrupt the witness's evidence about. It's a matter on which you can comment in due course. But it's no matter for objection. Yes, Mr. Groome. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me finish, please. If the witness is giving a statement, he certainly does not make the summary. You would not allow me to question him regarding the Patriotic League of people, though, in the summary under point 5 he speaks about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't know what your objection is. You're making a speech. What is it that you want to say, and make it clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In answer to my questions about the Patriotic League of people, he says: "I don't know that." And here in the summary he says the league founded by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is it that you are asking us to do?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking for an investigation into who compiles these things which later prove to be contradictory in the evidence of the witness. And he is not the first witness. This applies to a host of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We hear what you say. Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's very often the case that witnesses, when confronted with statements that are several years old, they may have different memories at that time. They may have made a mistake. Very often the procedure which is followed in taking the statement, the witness never sees the statement in their own language. It's read to them through an interpreter. These are all fair matters for cross-examination. Mr. Milosevic has fully exploited that, and it's a matter for the Chamber to consider what it considers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I wasn't going to invite you to respond, but anyway, you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: These are matters which of course the accused can raise in due course when it comes to considering the weight to be given to witnesses. These are lengthy statements, and it's not uncommon for witnesses to have different recollections. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just ask for a private session for the first few questions I have to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-1493, Mr. Milosevic put to you that Arkan came to Bijeljina at the invitation of Mauzer and the local leadership. Let's assume for the purpose of my question that that is a true fact. My question to you is: If that were to be true, does that lessen or negate the obligation that the JNA had with respect to this incursion of armed men into the Bijeljina area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's assume that Arkan was called to Bijeljina by Mauzer, and he was also a special illegal unit. That does not lessen the obligation on the part of the chief of the staff of the 2nd Military District to react and to have these -- to take measures against these persons who came in from another state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milosevic put a question to you. I'm going to read the question and then read the answer. Then I want to ask you a follow-up question. Mr. Milosevic's question was the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the JNA the sole legitimate armed formation and I would like to emphasise the word legal, lawful. Your answer was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army was the sole legal armed force on the territory of Yugoslavia. Now it appears that both you and Mr. Milosevic agree on this point. My question to you is the following: Did the JNA or the command of the JNA that covered the areas of Serbia in which men like Arkan, in Erdut, and Seselj were gathering men together, arming them and training them before they were sent into Bosnia, did the JNA in that area also have the obligation to deal with these armed formations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA -- first of all, those units were trained in JNA centres. They were trained by JNA officers, and the JNA prepared them, to all intents and purposes, for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in violation of the laws and regulations governing the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1493 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fully, because the Yugoslav People's Army did not have the right to train or arm units which were not within its formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-1493, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, while we're waiting for the next witness, let me mention the next selection of Croatia 92 bis witnesses which we'll deal with. They relate to Skabrnja, Knin, Jajce camp and Vocin. And I've noted in chronological order C-1072, 1073, 1102, 1160, 1166, 1186, 1192, 1202, and 1205, and we'll take those at a convenient time, if possible this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll try perhaps to deal with that tomorrow. And it may be convenient tomorrow if I deal with the question of disclosure of materials generally. I'll be in a position to do that then. The next witness is an open-session witness, so the Court should be adjusted. It's Morten Torkildsen. I'll for the public record set out what the position is about his reports, but the Chamber will require, of course, to follow only his second report and an index of exhibits. I intend to deal with perhaps a dozen exhibits very briefly in what I hope will be a succinct examination-in-chief of the witness. There being a full report, there was no need or, it seemed to me, utility in providing a further summary. And while the witness is coming in and for the benefit of journalists and others who may be familiar with the overall material, they should know that the witness Morten Torkildsen filed or the Office of the Prosecutor filed in respect of the witness two reports, a first report which related to Kosovo, which is not, by order of the Court, to be given in evidence, although three documents from it are to be admitted, and they will be added to the documents produced by the second report. The second report deals with Croatia and Bosnia, and I will present some parts of that on the overhead projector. But otherwise, those viewing, in particular the journalists, will have to take advantage of seeing the fully produced report if they want the detail of the matters into which we are inquiring. In addition to those materials, there is a curriculum vitae of the witness. It was served with a filing of the 21st of June. For convenience, I'll lay one or two pages of that on the overhead projector as I take him very briefly through his experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: While we're waiting, it might be convenient to deal with the exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And get an exhibit number, the next Prosecution number for the expert report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P426.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the registry and Ms. Wee have cooperated in the way the exhibits should be produced, and also your legal officer Gideon Boas. We have an exhibit list which takes account of the decision of the Chamber, and I should make this point clear as well for the benefit of those who may have seen the whole report. The Chamber excluded from consideration one or two paragraphs from the second report. I'll deal with that as we go through. And in light of, therefore, the deletions from the second report, the admission from the first report of three exhibits, it seemed helpful to have a comprehensive index which I hope is before you. That index takes us through 61 tabs. I beg your pardon. Sixty-five. Thank you very much. And I'm in the Court's hands as to whether the exhibit index and the associated exhibits should simply become part of the same exhibit 426 or whether they should be separate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think the report should be separate. It might be more convenient to have a separate bundle. Is that what is proposed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That would certainly -- well, at the moment, the only thing against that is if you look at the index itself, the very first exhibit on the index is the second report. So that part matters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So it doesn't seem to be on the wit of man to have Exhibit 427 as the next exhibit and just don't bother about tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. 427 is the exhibit. And the curriculum vitae maybe we can put in as 428.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can we have the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And in all cases, I will hope to have the witness having a copy of the document in front of him with the usher placing the relevant pages of a parallel document on the overhead projector where appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the copy of the overhead projector become our Exhibit 428 go on -- on the overhead projector. Copy of the curriculum vitae go on the overhead projector, become our Exhibit 428. Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 1 of that, Mr. Torkildsen, revealed that you received a master of science in shipping, trade and finance; Paragraph 2, you earned a bachelor of science in management sciences from the University of Manchester; Paragraph 3, you've since 1989 been professionally involved in auditing financial transactions; Paragraph 4, 1989 to 1992, senior auditor with the auditor department with the city of Oslo; Paragraph 5, senior investigation officer from 1992 to 1994 with the Norwegian directorate of taxes, conducting various detailed investigations; Over the page, paragraph 6, please. Sorry. We're moving fast but this is material the Chamber has seen so it's really for the public side of the trial, the public character of the trial. Paragraph 6. From October 1994 to April 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, that's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Wrong page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The usher can find the declaration of Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've only got two pages out of three for some reason. Take those two pages and I'll have to follow them from the ... From October 1994 to April 2000, the special investigator with the Norwegian National Authority for Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Environmental Crime. And we can see by scanning it the scale of the investigations you had to investigate there, following money trails in the work that you did. It's perhaps worth noting at the foot of what we can see on the screen that in the course of this work, you were granted particular powers by the United Kingdom government; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next paragraph. You then had to deal with a major corruption case involving UNICEF. You set that out in paragraph 7 of this curriculum vitae.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 8 and over the page, please. The top of the page, please. Thank you. You were then a tax auditor in Norway, directing police in their financial investigations?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And paragraph 9, presenting your reports in court. And then from January 2000 until the present, you've been a financial investigator, one of the very limited number at most of financial investigators working in this institution for the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in preparing the reports that have been presented to the Court, you've reviewed more than 10.000 pages of materials in order to reach the conclusions you have.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Probably a lot more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I can have those pages back so that I don't mislay them. May the witness have a copy of his second report, and usher, I'm going to ask if you be so good as we go through pages of report with the witness, if you'd lay the corresponding pages on the overhead projector so that they may be viewed. If he could have a copy himself and here comes another one for the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, I'm only going to ask a comparatively limited number of questions, perhaps half an hour's worth, we'll see. But if we go to page 3 at the bottom of your report, paragraph II, summary of conclusions. Having reviewed the materials you did review --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Did you conclude that the "SFRY and/or the Republic of Serbia provided financial and material support to the Serb-controlled districts in Croatia between 1991 and 1995 and in Bosnia-Herzegovina between 1992 and 1995"?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. When going through the documents, I have seen no other source of external financing for the RS and the RSK than the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 6. Was that support directed towards Serb military units and Serb civilian government organs established in those areas?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking the form of direct financial assistance, military equipment, food, personnel, and expertise?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 9. In your judgement, given your expertise, did you conclude as a strong conclusion that funding for the army of the Republika Srpska and the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina, known for the purposes of your report and generally as the VRS and the SVK, came from a single financing plan for all three Serb armies?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 10. The SFRY provided assistance, financial and material, to the VRS and the SVK by providing military material and also by paying the salaries of the officers in those armies?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also deal with budget deficits. Just a word about that. Can you explain that to us in a sentence?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Basically the -- the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, short named the FRY, was covering the budget deficits of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 11 sets out this view that to facilitate this support from the SFRY the economies of the SFRY, the RS, and the RSK were organised into a structure that can be described as an economic and monetary federation. Now, is that a term of art that you have coined? A term of art. A term you have coined or is it a term that find any expression in any other literature?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is partly an expression that's mentioned in some of the documents, but it's also obvious particularly from one of the exhibits attached to this report, the so-called report by Mr. Miletic who was a director at the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's a -- that's the one report I think that's been excluded. No, the report's included?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The report is included, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So it's partly your own phrase but it's also reflected elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. But it's obvious from the documentation attached to this report that it was a monetary union and something similar to an economic federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 12, you deal with terminology that you use throughout the report of a primary issue, but you match that here to the phrase "printing money." Can you just give us a sentence or so on that conclusion? And we'll probably look later at the economic and financial consequences of the use of primary issue, but can you just explain these terms?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The -- in simple terms, the phrase "primary issue," would mean a credit done by the National Bank of Yugoslavia and basically the printing of money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 11 -- beg your pardon. Paragraph 13. It's going to be tab 11 which we'll want to display. No. Sorry. Paragraph -- as I was. Paragraph 13, you deal with the Serbian Ministry of Defence, and you say that it played a major role in financing and providing of equipment. There was a document I wanted you to look at just to remind the Judges. It's this one here. Thank you very much. The Chamber may recall this document, I think, coming through C-032 on the 10th of March. Just have a look at it, please. Can it be placed on the overhead projector? The Chamber will remember the document probably because of its colourful presentation. Now, this is a document I think which you hadn't -- it hadn't come to your attention until yesterday in the way things work out.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. I had never seen this document before I was shown it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: C-032, meaning Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't C-032.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I've got the microphone off because I'm not sure. I just want to be quite sure the witness was in open session. I'm sure he was, but I just want to check on the name. But I'll come back to the name of the witness. We'll look at the document because the Chamber will recall it and I haven't made out His Honour's naming of the witness is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're looking at the document, your conclusion therefore drawn well before this document was produced in evidence was that the Serbian ministry of defence played a major role in financing and providing military equipment at the Serb-controlled districts in Croatia, and you said this, Mr. Torkildsen: "Such a task was not conducted by the Serbian MOD alone because it possessed no stocks of military supplies. Rather the aid occurred with the executive assistance and the cooperation of the JNA VJ". Now, yesterday when you saw this document without having the transcript of the witness's - relevant witness's - evidence drawn to your attention, the document was explained to you and the witness producing it was in open session, Miroslav Djordjevic. Does this document match your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it does, because based on my -- the documents I have reviewed, I can see that the Serbian Ministry of Defence received a lot of requests from the various Serb-controlled districts in Croatia in 1991 and 1992, and the way that I understood it is that no Ministry of Defence do themselves possess the military hardware or financial means. And that means that basically they haven't got -- must have forwarded these requests to the JNA who were sitting on the military hardware. And also when it comes to financial assistance, the Serbian Ministry of Finance must have been involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then back to paragraph 14 of your report. You speak of a large number of documents showing decisions regarding the support to the Serb-controlled districts in Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, were made by the highest-ranking military and political leaders of the SFRY and the Republic of Serbia. Do you particularly refer to what may go on the overhead projector or in part may go on the overhead projector C4682, tab 11 of what is now our Exhibit 427. If you take us to what you believe to be the relevant part of this, please, or summarise its effect for us, Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Basically these -- these are the minutes of a meeting between the accused and the leadership of the RSK, including Goran Hadzic and Milan Martic. In this meeting, they are planning for the financial needs of the RSK, for the army, and the police in the coming year, 1993, and also for the two remaining months in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The Chamber has, I think, already seen this document produced through another witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Back to your report. Paragraph 15. You conclude as follows: "When the JNA pulled out of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the second half of 1992, it left the Serbs there with a nearly complete army supplied with the remains of the JNA's 2nd Military District." And you referred to quotation of Mladic in a report of December 1992, "Our army is one of the rare ones in history to have started a liberation war with a very solid material base especially as concerns combat hardware, ammunition, and food reserves." And you say that that particular remark is supported by the written statement made by the accused which we can find in our 4C, which is now tab 3. Thank you very much. On the ELMO, please, if we can. Can you look at this, please, Mr. Torkildsen, on the overhead projector. Take us to the passage of significance?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It's the passage on the second page of the translation. I think you have gone to the third page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And in particular, the second paragraph starting with "As regards the resources spent for weapons, ammunition and other needs of the army of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, these expenditures constituted a state secret and because of state interests could not be indicated in the Law on the Budget, which is a public document. The same applies to the expenditures incurred by providing equipment, from a needle to an anchor, for the security forces and special anti-terrorist forces in particular, from light weapons and equipment to helicopters and other weapons which still remain where they are today, and this was not made public because it was a state secret, as was everything else that was provided for the army of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this of course was the statement that the accused made when he'd been detained and in respect of his detention; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. It's dated the 2nd of April, 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's one of the three documents filed with the first report which that was admitted into evidence by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With those conclusions, we'll look at a limited number of paragraphs of your report before I sit down, and if we can have in mind the structure of your report. On page 5, Roman III, you dealt with the financing of the JNA between 1992 -- 1991 and 1992. The passage was only a few pages. If we could turn to the next page, page 6, paragraph 19, just for amplification. In dealing with this topic, you refer to the transcript of a Presidency meeting held on the 21st of August, 1991, where there was a discussion about the lack of revenue in the SFRY budget and financing of the JNA. And you then set out the view of Ante Markovic, president of the SIV. Remind the Chamber what the SIV was and Ante Markovic's position and summary again what is contained in 19 and over again to the quoted passage.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Markovic was the last prime minister of the SFRY. And the SIV, that's the federal Executive Council. What they are discussing here is basically the financing of the SFRY budget at the time. The problem was for the SFRY budget was that the different republics were pulling out, and they were no longer contributing towards the federal budget, meaning that they had to find other means of financing. And the only alternative they had was to get their finances through the National Bank of Yugoslavia, and that means primary issues. They basically printed money to finance the federal budget.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The relevant quotation can be seen over the page at page 7. One of the advantages of this document having been served publicly or filed publicly is that the sharp eyed have been able to draw to attention anything that may be in error. Your report faithfully sets out the translation received by you of the names Pelivan, but in fact there is an inconsistency between the name Slobodan Pelivan and Jure Pelivan which should be corrected by the replacement of which name?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It should read Jure Pelivan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On both occasions. That's on page 7 towards the top, but you were simply setting out what was the actual translation that was provided to you.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We move on for those viewing who may have seen the full document. It's important to observe at page 9, at paragraph 23, which runs over to page 10, has been excluded from consideration. On page 10, and therefore come to paragraph 24 under the broad heading, Roman IV, "The creation of a monetary federation and its impact on the financing of the Serb-controlled districts in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina." The largest passage of your report, I think. Of this we need perhaps focus on a few paragraphs. If we go to paragraph 30, and perhaps you'd be good enough really to summarise for us your paragraphs 30 and 31, there being no documents I wanted to draw to the Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: What basically happened regarding the restructuring of the banking industry was that the RSK and the RS established their own national banks that were both subordinated to the National Bank of Yugoslavia. And through this coordination and subordination, primary issues were made available for the RS and the RSK. And it's sort of is monetary integration and monetary union was at this final stage in the beginning of 1994 where they eventually got the same currency across the three regions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Usher, if you'd be good enough to go to page 13, paragraph 37. Again there being no documents to look at on this occasion, perhaps you could summarise that for us, Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, this monetary union that was created made sure that money was made available for the RS and the RSK. And it also made sure that the major vehicle to make this money available, the so-called SDK, the public accountancy service was in operation throughout the whole RS, RSK and the FRY this was tied together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll see a document shortly that deals with the importance of SDK, but if we now go over the page, usher, to page 14, paragraph 39. At paragraph 39, Mr. Torkildsen, you record reviewing a report, part of 4769, written by Milivoje Miletic, then director of the National Bank of Yugoslavia who was stationed at the NBRS. Expand for us NBRS?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That's the National Bank of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the 4th and the 8th of April, 1994. And with those experiences to hand, Miletic analysed the restructuring of the national banking systems and indeed set out three stages for the restructuring. This is the one paragraph where I think several exhibits can usefully be looked at and in a sequence. Thank you very much. Thank you. First tab 32, C4712. And while that document's coming to the overhead projector, the Chamber may wish, in order to save time, to look on to paragraph 111 at page 40 where the same document is referred to and I'll just read what it says there of the document before the witness take us to any details of it he wants to particularly bring to our attention. The document is dealt with at paragraph 111, describing it as the "Analysis of combat readiness and activities of the army of the Republika Srpska in 1992, dated April 1993. The report demonstrates the extent to which the VRS was supported by the FRY and the JNA in 1992 and 1993." Mr. Torkildsen, with that summary and the document on the overhead projector the places where you want to draw our attention?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: If you can go to page 128, please. And at the bottom of this page. Basically the whole report is a report on the activities of the Republika Srpska army in 1992, and there is a section within this report on finances as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If anybody following in the B/C/S version, it's at page 112, I think.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And there's an amount mentioned at the bottom of the page which is actually the planned expenditure for the RS army in 1992, and it reads 53 billion dinars. Not accurate, but let's leave that. If you can please go to the next page. And just to mention that the RS army budget was, of course, part of the whole budget for the RS, as it is in any country. And you can see on the top of the page there what they had actually spent by -- by February 28, 1993. They had spent more than 81 billion dinars. And further down there, it's actually a breakdown of what these expenditures are. And we can see that personnel outlays accounts for more than 50 per cent of the total expenditure. And by personnel outlays, it's basically salaries for the conscripts and other support for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I also think if we go to the next page we will see the number of soldiers, conscripts, in the RS army in 1992. Yes, it's mentioned there. It's actually -- it reads that the budget was drawn up for an army which should have numbered 100.000 soldiers, while its average strength was actually 212.000, 212.000 troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reference there to hyperinflation, do you want to deal with that now or later, and its consequences on the economy and finances generally?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: If we can take that later, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything else on this document or is that the purpose for which you require it in amplification of what's in your written report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: As mentioned, this army budget was part of the budget of the RS, and I have reviewed the -- actually, the RS annual accounts for 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is one of the new documents, I think that, that's been produced, and the order in which you would like to review them is C5358, tab 59. This was a document added to your original report, coming from the Official Gazette of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is actually the budget for 1993. I mean, we can look at that now, but I was actually referring to the --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Annual accounts for 1992. But since this is on the overhead now, what is mentioned here is that the original income of the budget is a rather small amount compared to the total budget as you will see here. And as you also can see under Article 2 is it is mentioned credits in the amount of 729, something, and the term "credit" in this respect means primary issues. This is the money originating from the National Bank of Yugoslavia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may be necessary just to justify that observation. What does a credit in this setting mean primary issue, which is printing of money?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: If we go -- if we can have the Miletic report on the overhead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. That's 4712 again, tab 32.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Nice. That's the wrong -- it's actually exhibit labelled 4769.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 4769, yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: And it should be the first document attached to that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the tab number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tab 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tab 14, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And go a bit -- it's the paragraph that starts with "The first phase of the operations of the National Bank of Republika Srpska ...". And further down it's mentioned that "It was normal to issue primary money on the basis of previous experience coming primarily from the National Bank of Yugoslavia." And going a bit further down there, it's stated that: "Among other things, from the second half of 1992 and onwards, primary money was issued through banks and the budget so that on the 31st December 1992, the balance of primary issue credits were 77.8 billion dinars. About 14.3 per cent of these credits, or 11.1 billion dinars, were given through the banks, while the remaining 85.7 per cent or 66.7 billion dinars were given for the budget of the Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All primary issue money distributed in two identified different ways. Any significance in the different ways that the money's being provided?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No. I mean, the money was basically given to cover the budget deficit of Republika Srpska, because they did not have original income or, basically I mean taxes to cover their expenditure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the credits that we saw on the previous document, justified by you, as amounting to primary issue printed money from this document.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. And if we go back to that document, the -- this revised budget for 1993, you will also see that almost all of it went to the RS army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The exhibit we're looking at at the moment features in your report at paragraphs 45 and 50. To save time, we might just remind ourselves what's said there. Is there anything else you want to say about the document while it's on the overhead projector at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We draw from it in your report at paragraph 45 that the programme described by Miletic created a single monetary region to include the FRY, the RS, and the RSK coming into effect in March 1994. The National Bank of the Republika Srpska commended by Miletic because, "As legal tender, the new dinar functions fully in the territory of the Republika Srpska." Anything you need to add to that or is that sufficient for your purposes?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, at that time they had the common currency for all three regions and that was the currency issued and controlled by the National Bank of Yugoslavia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you pick the point up again at page 18, paragraph 50 of your report where you refer to the minutes of the May 1994 meeting of governors, 4779, also appearing as 4769, where the minutes mention that the three banks operate as the main branches of the Yugoslav National Bank -- sorry, the two banks, and the two banks implement decisions of the national bank, and then the governor of the National Bank of Republika Srpska and the governor of the National Bank of Republika Srpska Krajina are required to attend sessions of the council of the Yugoslav National Bank without voting right, thus reinforcing your conclusions, if it was needed for you to make those conclusions, about complete integration?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was integration, and it was very much a subordinate relationship, meaning that the RS and the RSK national banks were subordinated to the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think in this sequence -- I'm sorry for having got the first two documents in the inconvenient order for you. I think you would like to go, correct me if I'm wrong, to B4647 next, which -- tab 30, thank you very much. Tab 33, which is a decision by the Republika Srpska on taking an out a loan from the National Bank to pay for the needs of the republic. Your comment on this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. Again the -- there was not enough money in the budget of the Republika Srpska, so they had to take out a loan from the National Bank. But when I'm referring to the National Bank here, I'm referring to the National Bank of Republika Srpska. But the money that they lent to the budget of the RS did originate from the primary issues given from Belgrade. And the amounts more or less fits in with what is mentioned in the report by Mr. Miletic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say more or less, the difference in amount, can you just remind the Judges of the figures, if you can remember them, to show how much it is more or less?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I think the figure mentioned by Miletic was 66.8 billion dinars, but here it is mentioned an amount of 56 billion dinars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: When you get to a convenient moment, it's quarter past.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing more you want to say about the document at the moment, Mr. Torkildsen?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The only thing I want to say is if you look at the interest rate, I think it's mentioned a bit -- it's mentioned 5 per cent per year. That means that this loan was basically a gift, and it's going to be paid down effective as of 15/12/98, meaning due to the hyperinflation, when you actually pay this back you would pay back nothing. For instance, in September 1993, the inflation had reached an enormous amount per month. I think at that time, the one Deutschmark was actually the equivalent of 86 million dinars. So even if this is a huge amount at that time in 1992, when it comes time to paying this back, it was worth nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those conclusions can also be found at paragraph 76 of your report in summary form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now for 20 minutes. Mr. Torkildsen, would you remember, please, in this and any other adjournments there may be during your evidence not to speak to anybody about it, and that includes the members of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Torkildsen, we've already looked when looking at your overall conclusions briefly at this document, tab 11, C4682, but looking at the body of it, it being a conversation with the accused, there may be some further comments you want to make on it. We see in the paragraph on the screen the accused Milosevic recorded as accepting the concept of forming the defence system of the Krajina on the basis that is set out there. I don't want to take time reading all of it, although I want to go to the financial bit at the end. Any comments you want to make on this page?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, the last sentence in this paragraph that this will be accomplished through the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go to the foot of the page, please. Usher, could we go to the foot of the page, please. "The problem of ensuring of the planned means for this year was brought because the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia does not have enough money inflow." I think. Can we then to the next page. "The president of the government of the Republic of Serbia was to intervene so the means could be delivered and he accepted it. "Based on the above-mentioned requests, I asked the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Serbia to plan the necessary means for financing the defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in 1993 to ensure the inflow of the means in this year and that would be 200 millions till the end of the month, and 150 till the 5th of December." Any comment?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I only comment that this problem of financing was obviously solved through primary issues. One of the exhibits, the RSK budget for the first half of 1993 clearly indicates that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, this is a record of a conversation involving the accused, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see the Republic of Serbia specified here rather than a federal body.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct, but obviously there must have been some sort of cooperation between the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia that I do not know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We passed over, my error, tab 65, the Republika Srpska's annual account for 1992, and I think there was a comment you wanted to make on that.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: If we have a look at Article 1 here, it is mentioned here an amount of total generated income in the amount of 18 something, and we can see that the total expenditure is much higher than that. And you have something called uncovered expenditure in this Article, and the uncovered expenditure here would basically be covered by primary issues. I would then like to refer back to the loan that was taken up on the 8th of August, 1992, that was shown on the overhead earlier on. And I would also point out the budget for -- or actually the revised budget for 1993 that was shown here as well. This all indicates that this was financed through primary issues, the uncovered expenditure. And also, I would like to highlight the Miletic report where he estimates that 66.8 billion dinars was put forward into the budget of the RS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 64 next, please, which is the RSK budget for 1993, one of the two -- one of the new -- three new documents that have been produced today. Your comment on this please, significance?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: First I would like to make the comment that this is a budget and not an annual statement, meaning that it's a plan for their finances for the first half of 1993. And it's mentioned here that the funds for the territories under the UN protection in the amount of -- I think it reads 609 billion dinars are obtained from additional funds of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And in addition to this, we have the National Bank credits in the total amount of -- well, it's even higher. It probably reads 2.231 billion dinars, meaning again primary issues. And as a total, I think that these two budget items actually finance more than 90 per cent of the total budget for that period. And if we can go further down on this document, please. Next page. A bit further down is a post called expenditure. Yes, there. And as we can see, most of the -- or actually about two-thirds of the expenditure planned for in this budget goes for funds for education and self-protection. It is specified military salaries covering about one-third of the salaries. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tab 63 next, the FRY's 1993 budget. I think we may be missing the first page of the English translation, but I hope you will be able to -- no, we're missing it here in court. Providing the passage that the witness wants is not on the first page, we will be all right. Mr. Torkildsen, can you survive with what we have?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: This budget is merely to illustrate that the method of financing in the FRY was the same in this budget. It's not actually a budget. It's the actual annual accounts, I think, for 1993, and it shows that more or less the whole budget or annual accounts of the FRY for 1993 were financed through primary issues. And it also shows that most of the -- this budget goes for the army, meaning the VJ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you -- did you look for, in the budgets of the FRY and in their annual accounts, postings of sums in respect of the armies of the RS and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have looked for that, but I have found no budget posts in the FRY budgets indicating that they were funding the RS or the RSK army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your judgement, is that consistent with that which the accused said in his document relating to his detention about the necessity for secrecy of these funding procedures?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The only post I managed to find in this -- in these FRY budgets is actually a post somewhere mentioning funds for the UN protected areas. But that's just a very small amount, or actually, a small percentage of the total budget. In my view, that could not have gone to the RS army or the RSK army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go back to your report. There are only a couple more exhibits to look at and then I shall be done. On the report itself we were on page 14, paragraph 39. I've swept up several of the references I would have otherwise taken you to. We can pass on, I think, just to paragraph 53 on page 19. You've dealt with this in part already, but it may be helpful and perhaps helpful if put in conventional or homely terms just to explain what the SDK system was and what it could be likened to and what it facilitated.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: First, it's basically a transfer system for settling financial transactions. And it also had an auditing control function. So basically the primary issues were channelled through the SDK system when they were made available for the RSK and the RS. But also in the documents there are a lot of mentioning about problems with the SDK system. It was not functioning all the time. Just to highlight that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Those of us broadly familiar with electronic transfers to banks or whatever it may be, this was such a system but with particular objectives in mind?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Well, it was something similar, but I don't know the technicalities of how this worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you've set out at paragraph 56 at the foot of page 19 of your report the view taken of it in a speech by Karadzic at the plebiscite of the Serb people on the 1st of November, 1991, where at the top of page 206 your report he made this point in reflect of the significance of the system: "Be prepared soon to take over the SDK decisively. I mean, to appoint your own man in the SDK. Prepare the ground, first talk to them, ask them whether they're ready to work in a moment that is not legal, in accordance with the laws and regulations which you, as the municipality authority, will give them." Any significance about that beyond what is stated there by Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Basically the SDK system must have been of paramount importance to be able to conduct transactions, whereas the only alternative would have been cash payments. Just reflecting on our own system, I mean, if everything was to be settled in cash, of course it would have created enormous problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To page 22 of your report, please, paragraph 62, and tab 24, B3501 I may have missed one tab we have to look at, but let's go to tab 24, B3501. At paragraph 62, you refer to the decision by the government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 14th of May, 1992, regarding the use of funds available from the primary issue. The document is now on the overhead projector. Your additional comment? You can see it all set out probably on page 22 of your report, but your comment?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's actually set out in paragraph 62 here. I mean, the most important thing is that the primary issues will be used in accordance with the decisions of the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And nothing more to be said about it than that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: At -- at that time, the National Bank of Republika Srpska was not created yet, and it was obviously that these primary issue were given directly from the NBY and not through the National Bank of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You draw attention at page 25 your report, paragraph 72 to one particular documents which we needn't look to, although it's been exhibited before. Document C4830, or properly tab 18 of 352. A request for cash from the National Bank of Republic of Serb Krajina, to the National Bank of Yugoslavia authorising a grant of cash in the sum of 10 million dinars, then equivalent to 10 million Deutschmarks. Any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. It shows that the National Bank of Republika Srpska Krajina was still even in 1995 requesting cash from the National Bank of Yugoslavia. I'm not saying that they got this from a gift, but at least the NBY is the provider of the cash here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as we come to the end of your passage of your report on financing of the JNA, those viewing it familiar with the total document should know at page 27 and onwards that paragraph 79 and then through paragraph 80, 81, 82, and 83 are being excluded from consideration by the Chamber. So that brings us on page 30 of your report. To a paragraph headed "Inflation and the value of the Yugoslav dinar." Again, this may not be the most convenient place, lest I should forget it, can you make the comments you can make about the linkage of primary issue or printing of money, inflation and hyperinflation and the effect that that had?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The effect it had is basically set out in the two appendixes to this report, appendix A and B, showing how the value of the dinar was devaluated compared to the Deutschmark. As I pointed out in September 1993, one Deutschmark was worth the equivalent of 80 -- 80 something million dinars. It's also said by economists that primary issues would be very much be the equivalent of an extra tax on the people. It's like transferring wealth from the citizens to the state, because it's the state whose possession of the means and the result of the primary issues. They are actually increasing their money on behalf of the citizens who are still left with the same money. So it's definitely a transfer of wealth from the citizens to the state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this case used substantially, very substantially, for funding the armies and the other governments in the way that you've revealed.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw at an earlier stage a divergence of opinion between the accused and Ante Markovic about these matters. The effect of hyperinflation generated through the printing of money on an economy, is that something that is well known and well recorded in standard literature?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean, there is lots of articles on this issue. I would just like to say one thing regarding the -- I have tried to convert a lot of the dinar sums that are mentioned in this report into Deutschmark, but I think that these conversions should be read very carefully, because it's very difficult to do a calculation in periods when we are talking about hyperinflation. I think the most important area is to look at the budgets and the relative proportions that's financed through primary issues and what the money actually went to, to the army. Look at the percentages there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 31 of your report, at paragraph 89, section Roman V, you deal with the assistance to the Serb-controlled districts in Croatia made by the Republic of Serbia. There's nothing I need you to, I think, amplify there. So we can go straight to page 39, paragraph Roman VI where I have just a couple of references to you under the heading "Assistance to the Serb-controlled districts in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina made by the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Paragraph 108 and following. And then at page 40, page 110, you set out an analysis by Mladic of the importance to the VRS of the support to the Serb-controlled districts in Bosnia-Herzegovina in an earlier report dated September 1992. Your comment on that and, if necessary, we can look at an exhibit but maybe survive without, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. My reason for including this is that the financial assistance provided which are described in several documents should be put into perspective. Of course, if we -- it's obvious here that Mladic is talking about the transformation of part of the JNA into the VRS. And of course if he had to convert this into financial terms, that would have been a huge amount of equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the page to 112. You deal with an analysis from, I think, the exhibit inferred from the previous page. Any comment on this or does it speak for itself?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's mentioning of -- of a letter of credit here, a sort a guarantee. And the sums mentioned have eventually had to be covered by -- by the primary missions. And the amounts mentioned there, I mean, it's mentioned soldiers' wages on the bottom here. And in document C4712, the wages to the soldiers were mentioned as well. I think we have already covered this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps the last documentary reference because I've skipped one or two will be C4752 which is tab 52 and page 42 your report, paragraph 116. This document, I think, is a memorandum we can see dated December of 93 by the Chief of Office of the SDK, Commander Cedo Radankovic for a meeting at the VJ General Staff and the coordination of tasks. What does it reveal to you, please, Mr. Torkildsen?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, which paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 116 and --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. This document basically shows that it was one single financial plan for funding all three armies, meaning the RS army, the RSK army, and the VJ. They are -- there's talk here about the financial requirements for all three armies and how much each of them should have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can find the quotation you've set out in your report. Perhaps you can point it to us if you can find it quickly where it says: "We have learned unofficially that the above total balance of requirements for 1994, the federal government will only be able to provide 850 million USD for all three armed forces instead of 3.29 billion." This indicates an overall and collective view. Is that the decision?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can find that on the document, do so.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: There is a footnote in the report here, but it's actually -- it's an ERN reference here, so --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Don't worry. It's there to be found. Yes. Thank you very much. I think in the circumstances, that's all I need ask you. Wait there, please. You'll be asked some further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The problem is that we don't have ERN number in our exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, if necessary, I'll find it, but I don't want to take time unnecessarily. I'll deal with it in a minute or later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's switched on now. I don't know whose fault it is, but so far I haven't had a chance to see any of these exhibits. So I'll ask you to bear that in mind. I won't be able to quote them, but I'll take it from my notes, the notes that I took down listening to the testimony. So I'll be able to comment and ask my questions based on those notes and what I heard. And I must say that my associate hasn't seen those documents either. Just before the break, the registrar handed me this batch of documents. Now, whether that arrived earlier or not, I don't know. However, there won't be any problems on that score, except perhaps I won't be able to tell you of the exhibit number, because as I say, I'm seeing all this for the first time what the witness has testified about but not to waste time. Could you tell me, please, how much time I will have at my disposal for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, why don't you make a start with the half hour available. We'll then consider how long you might need bearing in mind that there is a report for you to cross-examine on. But certainly into tomorrow when you will have a chance to look over the things with your associates and look at the new exhibits. If it's of any assistance, I would think something in the region of two hours, but that's merely an immediate resort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: To assist the accused he had all the exhibits in advance apart from three additional exhibits which were provided to him recently. And his associates have been provided with the notification of what the tabs would be so that it should be possible for them to compile the existing exhibits into a tabbed order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's by no means easy from experience to get the tabs and the numbers in line. Mr. Milosevic, will you, when you want to refer to a number, give it the C number if you've got it and then we can relate it to what's in the new exhibit bundle. But remember we need for the purposes of the record to make sure we identify it, so there may be a bit of time spent on that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is precisely -- that is precisely why I drew your attention to that. I said that I don't have the numbers. But as I can see that Mr. Torkildsen is able to find his way around this material very easily, it won't be difficult for me to comment on the contents of what he says and to clarify certain points having to do with the contents of the report. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Torkildsen, in your report you state that you graduated management, shipping, trade and finance, that those are your specialist subjects. Is that right? You graduated in those subjects?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: That's right. I do have a master's degree in shipping, trade, and finance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell me this, please. Do you have any qualifications whatsoever in law, and specifically as it relates to an assessment and evaluation of exhibits and evidence in court proceedings, for example?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I have no education in law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, you said and I'm quoting you: "I managed successfully to find, identify, and draw vital information with respect to financial documents, witness statements, and other documents." You say something to that effect. Can you tell us exactly the nature of the source of your information upon which you base your conclusions, and also to be more specific as to what you meant by saying that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is basically in-house documentation I have identified that's contained within the evidence system of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's fine. Now, tell me this: In your report, at least the one I read, I did not notice that you refer to any provisions of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and its member republics at all. Am I right in concluding that if I say you didn't use that source material, either constitutional or laws and bylaws, would I be right in saying that, in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I did use laws, because as far as I know, the budgets and the annual accounts are introduced as laws and published in the Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say constitutional laws, laws and bylaws, I'm not thinking of the laws governing the budget only, because the budget is adopted by the parliament. But I'm talking about the provisions, legal provisions from the constitution and the general provisions of the SFRY and its Member States. So apart from the budget, did you take a look at these other provisions, laws, bylaws, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you consider that you can have a complete analysis, a valid analysis of the financing of state organs for any particular state from the resources that same state disposes of if you don't include the legal norms governing financing as well as other relevant laws?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, because I think the budgets and the figures speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Without going into the details of the federal system of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, do you think that we can conclude -- legal system, I apologise. Did you reach the conclusion that is it is from the resources that make up legally the resources of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, would it be possible to finance the functioning of that same state regardless of what level, federal level, republican level, and of course to finance and put into practice certain -- these demands of the economy, that the economy makes?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the normal way of financing. A budget is, normally in any jurisdiction, is approved by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. And as far as you know, is there any country in the world, any state in the world which does not have an army and police force which are not financed from its public sources and revenues?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: At least I have not heard about such a country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask some more preliminary questions to clear up these matters. You -- as you yourself say, you used witness statements, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I did not use witness statements for this report. This is solely based upon documents. The report I provided on the Kosovo aspect of the financing was based upon witness statements and notes from interviews with witnesses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you. That means -- or let me ask you this: So you did use certain witness statements, didn't you? That isn't being challenged, is it? Are you disputing that?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I am, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's given his answer, Mr. Milosevic. He's used witness statements for the part that's been excluded, not for the part the evidence about which he's giving. He said he used the documents for that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you excluded those reports where statements were included. Is that right, Mr. May? You excluded that from the testimony; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think he means you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm excluded giving evidence about the Kosovo report. If I may correct myself. There's one witness statement or statements that's used in this report, and that is the appeal against your detention in your domestic case dated 2nd of April, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In fact, I misunderstood the accused. The answer is yes, we excluded the first report on -- which was based on the statements. It's one of the reasons we excluded it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. In the interest of this cross-examination, let us clear up one point. Does what mean, because even now in this batch that I received from the registry, it says "Second expert report of Morten Torkildsen." That is number one. Does that mean that this second report is included in what we have to discuss or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't follow you. The report which you should be dealing with are -- is headed "Second expert report." And as you know if you've been following, it is that concerned with Croatia and Bosnia. We're not concerned with the other report which we excluded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But could you please explain to me this report, Mr. Torkildsen? This is purely a technical matter. So this report which is headed amended report of expert witness Morten Torkildsen, ending with chapter VII, headed opinion, and pages 106, 107, 108 up to 111, is that report part of what we are reviewing now or has it been excluded from what we are reviewing now?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: In you're referring to the amended expert report for Kosovo, that one is excluded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't say Kosovo here. It says: "Amended report of expert witness Morten Torkildsen, 11th of July, 2001." There was a discussion with I don't know whom, and so on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's all been excluded, that. The one you should concentrate on is the second report dated the 18th of November, 2002.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. From the 18th of November, 2002. Unfortunately, I don't have that report here but never mind, I will follow my notes. I don't think this will cause major difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen -- very well. Thank you. At the very beginning of your testimony this morning or, rather, today, you spoke about the financing of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and you stated -- I'm now relying on only what you said here.
