I'm not referring to any written statement of yours but only to what you said here, and that is that Republika Srpska and the RSK were financed exclusively by the SFRY or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And I noted down your words. You did not see any other sources. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: The only other source I saw was the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina also had their own budgets and their own public revenues out of which those budgets were financed? Not in their entirety, that's true, but at least partially. Did you have those facts in mind?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that the Republic of Serbia had its own budget, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not the Republic of Serbia but the Republika Srpska. I'm talking about the Republic of Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that those two entities had their own budgets, and that's what I've been referring to today. We have seen on the overhead here several of the budgets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it at issue that both the Republika Srpska and the RSK had their own public expenditures and revenues, public revenues about which they decided at their own assembly meetings, again in the form of laws on the budget? Is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: It is not in dispute that they had their own expenditures, and it's not in dispute that they had their own revenues as well. It's -- but it's a fact that most of the revenues into the budget were provided by the FRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you said, that you didn't see any other sources except the FRY, cannot be accepted as being correct, because it is quite obvious that they had their own public revenues. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: They had their own public revenues, but they were very limited. For instance, in 1993, almost all of their revenues originated from primary issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The analysis that you carried out, did you place it within the context of the events which affected the economic situation within the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, or did you examine and analyse these things out of context, the law on the budget, the various provisions and items in FRY, in the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I made the analysis based on the documents that are attached to this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Torkildsen, are you aware of the fact that in 1992, already in the spring of 1992, sanctions were in force against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. It was actually enforced on the 30th of May, 1992, where a complete trade embargo was imposed by the UN on the FRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that in 1993, already in May 1993, after the Vance-Owen Plan was rejected, the most rigorous sanctions were introduced which completely hermetically closed the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I am aware that further sanctions were introduced. I do not remember the details about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that when those severe sanctions were introduced in 1993, which completely blocked in the economic, financial and every other sense the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, that this provoked immense economic damage. And already in the second half of 1993, it provoked this hyperinflation. Did you bear in mind this sequence of events?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I do not doubt that there must have been difficult times. I mean, I find it logical that these sanctions sort of enhanced the need for primary issues and the consequence of that, the hyperinflation that occur occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hyperinflation, as you say. And did you notice that this was ongoing? The hyperinflation started already in May or June 1993, and once the inflation percentages were hundreds of millions at the end of 1993, at the end of 1994 through a new set of measures the inflation was stopped and the economic situation stabilised?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware that the inflation was stabilised in probably January 1994 when Governor Avramovic of the National Bank of Yugoslavia actually pegged the dinar to the Deutschmark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It pegged it to the Deutschmark. And as you're a financial expert, do you know what in fact was the key decision which enabled the stability of the dinar? The key decision of that programme which was then implemented by the National Bank. But a key decision and a key feature of that programme.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I would assume that the key decision was to stop using primary issues to finance the budget deficits. And that's actually what happened as well, as far as I can see, from the -- for instance, the FRY budget that I have reviewed for 1994. It was rather a limited amount of the revenue in that -- for that year that originated from primary issues. I think it was less than 10 per cent. It was completely opposite to what had happened in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a correct answer, Mr. Torkildsen. So that the key decision was the political decision taken. Let me put it very briefly, that there would be no budgetary deficit financing through primary issue, that the deficit could not be financed through primary issue. Do you as an expert believe that in that way the stabilisation was actually effected?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that sounds reasonable to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said primary issue impoverishes people, the population. I think it is more correct to say, I hope, that inflation does that. For example, I remember a governor, an old governor of the National Bank of Italy many years ago, I've forgotten his name, he was already retired, and when he told me the policy of inflation is pursued by poor governments because they do not wish to be taken -- to be criticised by the trade unions or by the government. So inflation and not primary issue is one of the factors or, rather, the main factor. But inflation is an unjust factor which impoverishes people because it taxes more or less equally a poor man and a rich man. Isn't at that right, Mr. Torkildsen?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I don't totally agree with your analysis. Basically primary issues creates inflation. That is -- that is a fact, and that's actually what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is all very good if you are in an economics class, but perhaps you should pay a little more attention to those matters that affect the central issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A central issue that we have already addressed is that inflation was provoked by the sanctions introduced in 1992 and the even more severe ones in 1993 so that we rightly qualified them as a silent genocide. Would you agree with such a qualification or not as an economist, as a person studying finances?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I don't know if I would comment to a silent genocide, but I don't think that these inflation and primary issues was merely the result of the sanctions imposed, because also in 1994 there were sanctions and you did manage to finance your budgets for 1994 as well even if the income did not originate from primary issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That shows that we were capable of dealing with it. But in any event, the economy was functioning at a much lower level as you probably know precisely because of the sanctions. It was incomparably less developed as an economy, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, by I think what you're saying makes sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Torkildsen, you refer to some sort of an economic federation, a monetary union using those categories. So tell me, please, are you aware of the fact that Republika Srpska, the RS, and the RSK had their own central banks and that they printed their own money, that there was the currency of Republika Srpska printed by the central bank of Republika Srpska or, rather shall issued by the central bank of Republika Srpska and the currency of the Republic of Serbian Krajina issued by the central bank of the Republic of Serbian Krajina? Are you aware of those facts?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I am aware that in 1992 and 1993, the RS and the RSK had their own currencies and that these currencies were printed at the Topcider mint in Belgrade, the printing facility of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. And I'm further aware that these two currencies of the RS and the RSK, they're set at the parity with the Yugoslav dinar, meaning that one RSK dinar and one RS dinar was the equivalent of one FRY dinar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, surely as an expert you will agree that the place where currencies are printed is only of technical significance. The question of the issuance of money by both central banks is more important. The previous SFRY used to print currencies for some other states, which doesn't mean that we were issuing that money. You know that sometimes the currencies, the bank notes of a one country will be printed in another country because this is a purely commercial business, a commercial deal, a service done by another country. But what I'm saying is that it was issued by the central banks of the RS and the RSK, regardless of where those currencies were printed because they didn't have mints of their own. Surely you distinguish between those two things.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I distinguish between them to a certain extent, but obviously letting someone print your currencies is a form for technical support and also considering this monetary union that existed and that these currencies were sort of convertible with each other at -- on a one-to-one basis. And also the fact that the primary issues there provided by the national banks of Yugoslavia is a part of the same matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. It's about time we adjourned. You can ask one more question and then Judge Robinson has a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, it is not at issue that both the RS and the RSK addressed the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for assistance, and Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Montenegro and Serbs in the diaspora, so there is no dispute over that. It is not disputed either that they received such assistance. What is wrong if the RS and the RSK addressed Serbia or the FRY for assistance? What can be considered as wrong or impermissible in this activity? So what if they did? Who else could they address themselves to the FRY or Serbia or Montenegro, the two republics of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN
utterances.text: I totally agree with you, Mr. Milosevic. They had no one else to turn to so their only place for getting financial assistance would be the FRY or the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll do it tomorrow morning, but Judge Robinson has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, your report covers what period, what years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It covers the period 1991, including 1995. Between 1991 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On in that period, you were able to note support from the FRY for the budgets of the RS and the RSK. What I wanted to find out was whether you're able to do an analysis of the previous years, let us say from 1985 to 1991, and make a comparison as between the support which the FRY gave the budgets of the RS and the RSK with the supports during that specific period.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the 1980s and in 1990 and 1991, there did not exist any budgets for the RS and the RSK, so that would be difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now. Nine o'clock tomorrow morning, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of April, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
